summary: Add explicitly authorized graph-free remote native Start over the durable authenticated home session

replay.detail: Existing Observe/Stop command bytes and authoritative rows are retained. Start requires a new immutable payload and negotiated start-authorizations-v1 capability; a former unsupported bare Start cannot acquire authority.

schema.detail: The existing private session journal additively retains bounded Start authorization revisions, content digests, revocation and closure fences. Native producer entry/results remain in the existing local_runtime_starts custody table, including original predispatch refusal reasons. Canonical resource memberships add a nativeCustody reader arm; native physical changes use owner-local transactions and the existing durable publication queue. Live launch custody retains payloads through positive withdrawal or exact-generation Stop receipts and blocks reclamation.

rules.detail: Home graph validation seals declaration/publication identities, selected desired and launch tokens, helper lifetime, rollout permission, account/continuation selectors, checkout/render inputs and the original start intent. Admission rechecks the graph under its exclusive writer; the seat checks signed exact scope, epoch, immutable payload, authorization revision and cancellation in the serialized dispatch barrier without fleet graph reads. Physical workspace, launch-freeze, kernel/capacity, resource membership and native generation gates remain authoritative. Remote backend entry calls canonical local_sessions::admit_capacity inside the immediate transaction that commits dispatched=1, sharing ordinary starts' 4096-slot unsettled custody budget. Only cleanup_verified or producer_closed releases an unbound producer reservation, never result labels, logical retirement, leader exit or supersession. Graph changes and native helper lifecycle events trigger ordered withdrawal; no successor is admitted before exact terminal custody receipts.

compatibility.detail: Both enabled endpoints must negotiate start-authorizations-v1 and retained-withdrawal-v1. Existing unconfigured full nodes keep their graph preflight and native launch path. Current runtime-start readers route remote custody records to session recovery rather than graph adoption. Never roll enabled journals or unresolved nativeCustody memberships back to readers missing these fences; preserve state, drain the original epoch and roll forward.

downtime.detail: No production deployment, graph offload, fleet membership retirement or CPU saving is claimed. A lost session does not stop healthy native execution or authorize a fresh successor.

manual.detail: Opt in with an explicit Start operation in the matching selected grant. Before enablement, configuration and both session constructors reject grants exceeding the encoded signed Hello budget, including JSON escaping and actual fleet authentication. The guarded owner-local Unix starts route constructs graph-bound payloads; raw command admission revalidates supplied Start payloads. Host-local credentials and runtime configuration are resolved on the execution host; graph document bytes are immutable admitted artifacts, not mutable lookup instructions.

recovery.detail: Restart/reconnect replays the same stable execution and retained actual native incarnation. Backend-entered unknown work reconciles the original operation only after meaningful native provenance/liveness or cancellation progress; absence never permits another spawn. Initial command delivery atomically carries any retained withdrawal, so replay cannot launch already-revoked work. Concurrent valid withdrawals preserve the first seat/home intent. Exact Stop gates the original Start closure on the same positive native producer and resource finalization before replacement or reclamation. Inherited finite executions retire only their exact positively verified root, never their parent membership or sibling roots; only the immutable membership owner cancels the whole scope. Ordinary local Stop declarations route remote body records through this retained native/session lifecycle, including offline physical retirement, rather than graph adoption. Remote Stop of an ordinary full-node-produced native session finalizes its local custody without requiring a remote Start envelope, both live and after restart during finalization.
